summary: Native postinstall dropper with sandbox evasion and encrypted sibling payload
details: On install, package.json's postinstall script requires a shipped native addon (addon.node on Linux, addon_win.node on Windows) and invokes its init() function. The Linux addon contains sandbox/CI detection strings (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, CIRCLECI, SANDBOX, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, APPVEYOR, NETLIFY) and anti-analysis reads of /proc/1/cgroup, /proc/1/cmdline, /proc/self/status (TracerPid), and /proc/self/maps, and calls fork+setsid+execlp to daemonize. The addon references a sibling file via the format string '%s/.napi_cache' and a '/tmp/.%u' staging path. The shipped.napi_cache is a 13.7 MB high-entropy blob with no printable strings, consistent with an encrypted executable payload loaded and executed by the native stub at init() time. The package presents itself as a 'cache-helper' with a trivial JS entry and ships no legitimate functionality that would justify a native addon with CI detection, debugger detection, and a multi-megabyte encrypted blob.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
